suggestions: R10-CODEX-S1 (S1; dependency declarations and progress receipt). In DLT-14.4-P11 replace ISA-4.9 with DLT-11.5, DLT-17.5 and DLT-25.1 for the actual 0.8 fault disposition. In DLT-9.2-P11 and DLT-9.4-P3 cite ISA-5.4-P1 for budget tuples/validation: P3 is absent and P2 only says F >= 4. In DLT-11.3-P7 cite ISA-5.4-P1, ISA-4.2 and the retained DLT-25.2 code-10 wording item instead of absent P4. Also change the allocation-class citation in DLT-3.4-P29 from ISA-3.3-P8 (free) to P7 (new)/ISA-4.3, and the clean-release citations in DLT-8.7-P7/P8 from ISA-3.3-P9 (slice) to P8 (free). DLT-8.4-P3 should cite DLT-16.2-P11 and ISA-4.7-P1 for ARG forwarding; ISA-12.3-P2 in 0.8 is an error-composition rule, not the exact-argument binding rule from 0.9. Check all remaining references by content, not existence alone, and amend the progress claim that all 243 references resolve. The operative dialect rules already provide these obligations, so these citation defects do not establish S0.

R10-CODEX-S2 (S1; DLT-5.2-P13). Make the correlated atomic-transfer interpretation explicit with the sentence proposed under C2. A useful explanatory vector is an i8 cell initially 1 followed by atomicrmw uinc_wrap with limit 2: the complete atomic transfer has least fixed-point old/stored domain {0,1,2}. Treating its virtual icmp/add/select as independent ordinary PT3 unions can introduce values outside that set. A read-only probe of the current checker gives {0,1,2} for the atomic source but TOP for the explicitly expanded source. Different source syntax can legitimately receive different reference precision; this probe is not an execution disagreement or an S0 allegation. Document that distinction rather than changing PT3 globally. The existing failed-cmpxchg witness already establishes that an impossible successful store must not add the proposed new value.

R10-CODEX-S3 (S1; D14 evidence priority within b-dialect-spec-oxs). Add a checked small-width instance forced onto the sampled path by lowering the configured exhaustive threshold, plus an above-default-threshold admission case. Execute the emitted CC oracle/swap/inverse calls independently for forward and adjoint orientations, preserved IN/MEM_IN/ARG bindings, controls 0/1 and a superposed control, and verify the full final tuple and clean scratch. A bound below the recorded sound B_bound must produce T-BUDGET before mutation; sampling must never emit native qinplace proof authority. Keep this labelled sampled evidence with universal-inverse/sound-bound obligations, not a proof inferred from clean ancillas. This strengthens the deliberately open I03/I14 evidence closure; it is not a condition for accepting the specification text.

The D14 execution witness would strengthen C6 without narrowing admission or treating the disclosed staging backlog as a blocker.
summary: Accept draft 0.2.11 on the ruled ISA-0.8 compatible track. Round 9 had no blockers, so previous_status is empty. No new S0 semantic regression or spec gap was established. D14 retains both exhaustive/library native and sampled CC paths; D20 preserves and tests first-region-operand ordering; D21 implements actual atomic update/store propagation; D22 preserves metadata fallbacks and checker-owned strict-subdomain evidence labels while leaving 0.9 invocation binding on its migration track. The requested gate passed 2834/2834. Three nonblocking suggestions address target-version dependency citations, PT12 explanatory precision, and the priority of sampled-path execution evidence. The 33 disclosed evidence closures remain staging work, not claims of completed full-program validation.
